object_context: Child atom of NS-B1 for the unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes Clay (A) route. Assume v is a mild bounded ancient Navier–Stokes solution on R^3 x (-infinity,0) with the Albritton–Barker Type-I quantity I(v,q)<infinity. Identify an equation-specific inherited trace/tail property strong enough either to yield times t_k->-infinity with uniformly bounded global L3 norm, activating Albritton–Barker Theorem 1.2, or to activate another source-valid Liouville theorem. Purely functional implications from A+C+D+E alone are excluded by the NS-B1 sparse-tail calibration; the Navier–Stokes dynamics, pressure relation, local energy inequality, mild representation, or another proved dynamical structure must do the work.

equivalent_formulations: Bridge form: every mild bounded ancient Navier–Stokes solution with finite I possesses a backward sequence uniformly bounded in global L3.

Tail-tightness form: derive a dynamics-specific uniform control preventing infinitely replicated critical mass from escaping to spatial infinity strongly enough to produce an L3-bounded backward slice.
Alternative-Liouville form: instead of global L3, prove an inherited property P from finite I and the equation such that a source-valid Liouville theorem applies to the full ancient trajectory class.

Contrapositive research form: if a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I exists, then every attempted global trace/tail functional compatible with a chosen Liouville theorem must fail; identify the exact failure mechanism.
solved_analogues: Albritton–Barker Theorem 1.2: a mild ancient solution with uniformly bounded global L3 norm along a sequence t_k->-infinity is identically zero.
Koch–Nadirashvili–Seregin–Šverák: bounded ancient solutions are rigid in two dimensions and in selected axisymmetric settings, where additional structural controls are available.
near_solved_analogues: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák critical L-infinity_t L3_x regularity/backward-uniqueness route supplies a rigidity trigger once the global critical norm is available.
Albritton–Barker Lemma 2.5 gives one-way implications from several weak Serrin/critical hypotheses to finite I, but the reverse direction needed here is not supplied.
The NS-B1 sparse-tail calibration shows local scale-invariant functionals can stay bounded while global L3 diverges on every slice when the Navier–Stokes equation is removed.

explicit_disanalogies: The sparse-tail functional calibration is not a Navier–Stokes solution and cannot refute an equation-specific bridge.
Local parabolic Type-I control and global spatial L3 integrability live on different locality scales; no implication may be inserted without a theorem.
A fixed or periodic renormalized orbit assumption is stronger than finite I and cannot be smuggled into the trace/tail bridge.
Pressure is nonlocal, so a velocity-only local tail argument may miss long-range coupling.
An almost-periodic/minimal-element mechanism from another critical PDE cannot be transferred without a Navier–Stokes stability/minimality theorem.
Even a complete NS-B1a theorem would eliminate only the registered Type-I branch, not Type-II or the Clay root by itself.

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A system may obey a strict per-shard or per-window resource bound while total replicated state is unbounded across infinitely many shards; a global eviction, synchronization, or conservation mechanism is required to convert local budgets into a global inventory bound.
common_abstraction: uniform local budget does not imply finite global inventory
replication/escape across many locations is the missing coordinate
a dynamics-specific coupling can rule out otherwise legal independent local configurations
source_to_target_mapping: local shard/window budget -> A,C,D,E bound on a parabolic cylinder
replicated state across shards -> spatially separated critical-mass packets
total inventory -> global L3 norm of a time slice
eviction/synchronization rule -> Navier–Stokes diffusion, nonlinear transport, pressure coupling, and ancient mild dynamics
shared_constraints: local constraints are individually valid but do not sum automatically
the global conclusion requires control of interactions or accumulation across locations
a counterexample can be made by sparse replication when the coupling law is removed
disanalogies: Navier–Stokes is a nonlinear PDE with continuous space-time and nonlocal pressure, not a discrete storage system
there is no literal eviction protocol or conserved global inventory corresponding to L3
the analogy does not prove any tail estimate
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Search for an equation-specific anti-replication/tail-coupling mechanism rather than another local critical scalar bound.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Prove on mild bounded ancient Navier–Stokes solutions that the proposed dynamical mechanism quantitatively rules out the sparse-tail functional calibration or otherwise yields a source-valid Liouville trigger; failure on a PDE-consistent adversarial class refutes the transfer.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only structural analogy used to identify the missing local-to-global coordinate; no mathematical authority is imported.

analogy_scan_notes: The retained analogy is intentionally about local-versus-global accounting, not fluid intuition. It survives the mapping/disanalogy gate because the NS-B1 sparse-tail calibration explicitly realizes the uncoupled local-budget/global-inventory mismatch. Surface analogies to turbulence cascades were not retained without a quantified target mapping.
